title: Redwood Structured Output + Function Calling Demo - Novus Retail
summary: Redwood AE and SE demo structured output and function calling in JSON mode for Novus Retail. Demo covered JSON schemas, server-side validation, repair/guardrails, Console route configs, Optimize recommendations for batching and quantization, and function/webhook invocation workflows. Customer concerns: strict schema enforcement, latency targets for checkout flows, data residency and SOC2/KMS integration. Agreement to run a 2-week pilot with sandbox webhook integration and share security docs and pricing.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-01 15:00 PST
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Ravi Desai (Redwood), Priya Menon (Novus), Luca Rossi (Novus CTO), Samir Khan (Novus ML), Hannah Lee (Novus Security)

[00:00] Ethan Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro, I'm Ethan, AE at Redwood, and with me is Maya our SE and Ravi on solutions.
[00:12] Priya Menon: Hi thanks, excited to see how structured output works. We're trying to reliably extract order events from chat transcripts and then trigger downstream tools.
[00:23] Maya Chen: Great, we'll demo JSON mode, schemas and function calling/webhooks. We'll also show the Console for route-level configs and Optimize recommendations.
[00:35] Luca Rossi: High level constraint: we care about sub-100ms token latency for certain endpoints, and strict schema enforcement — we can't have malformed orders hitting our pipeline.
[00:50] Maya Chen: Understood. We'll show both client-side and server-side validation options and fallback policies. Redwood supports model variants and automatic fallback if strict validation fails.
[01:10] Samir Khan: Also curious about streaming — can we stream partial JSON and still validate?
[01:18] Ravi Desai: Short answer: yes, streaming is supported; we can stream tokens but we have an end-of-response validation step. We can also do incremental KV-cache friendly outputs if needed.
[01:35] Hannah Lee: Security question up front — do you support KMS integration for encryption keys and do you have SOC2?
[01:42] Ethan Park: We have SOC 2 Type II, and we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for Private deployments; for hosted we offer bring-your-own-key options and audit logs. We'll share the security pack after the call.

Summary section / quick demo setup:
[02:05] Maya Chen: Okay I'm going to share my screen — starting from the Console. Top-left you can see Projects -> Routes. We'll create a route 'orders-extract' with JSON schema enforcement enabled.
[02:25] Maya Chen: Here's the schema (example): order_id string, items array of objects with sku, qty, price, total numeric; shipping.address object, customer.email pattern. I'm enabling strict mode which will reject responses that don't validate.
[02:45] Priya Menon: If strict mode rejects, can we fallback to a best-effort model variant or send to manual review queue?
[02:55] Maya Chen: Yes you can configure fallback policies per route. For instance we can fall back to a more lenient model, or route to a retry queue — or call a 'review' webhook. We demo both.

Function / tool calling demo:
[03:20] Maya Chen: Next I'm switching to the function-calling example. We'll register a webhook endpoint in the Console, map the JSON schema to the function signature, and show Redwood invoking the tool when validation passes.
[03:40] Luca Rossi: Are the tool calls synchronous or async? We need idempotency for our downstream service.
[03:48] Ravi Desai: We support both. The call can be synchronous with retries and idempotency keys, or async with delivery guarantees and dead-letter queue.

Live transcript + schema enforcement example:
[04:10] Maya Chen: I'll paste a sample chat and run the extractor. (runs)
[04:25] Maya Chen: Watch the response — it's streaming back a JSON object. You can see tokens arrive, then at 04:38 the final validation executes.
[04:38] (screen) Response: {"order_id": "ORD-10234", "items": [{"sku": "TSH-RED-M", "qty": 2, "price": 19.99}], "total": 39.98, "shipping": {"address": "123 Market St"}, "customer": {"email": "alice@example.com"}}
[04:50] Maya Chen: Validation passed, Console shows a green check and the webhook was invoked.
[05:00] Priya Menon: Nice. What if model returns an extra field or wrong type?
[05:10] Maya Chen: In strict mode that fails validation. You can configure an automatic repair attempt by calling a secondary model that tries to coerce types, or set an auto-correct rule. We demo a 'repair' policy next.

[06:00] Maya Chen: Now switching to JSON mode with guardrails — I trigger a prompt that might produce ambiguous item quantities. The guardrail layer enforces item.qty to be integer >=1.
[06:20] (demo) Model returns qty as 'two' spelled out — guardrail caught it and rewrote to 2 using a deterministic post-processing step.
[06:35] Samir Khan: That rewrite is deterministic? We need reproducibility for legal reasons.
[06:42] Maya Chen: The repair is deterministic if you enable 'deterministic post-process' in Console; otherwise we log the repair with diff and provenance.

Performance & model variants:
[07:10] Ravi Desai: For latency you can route low-latency requests to our hosted low-latency pool or your Dedicated pool. For heavy batches, Optimize recommends quantized variants and batching configs.
[07:25] Luca Rossi: Do you provide cost estimates for those suggestions?
[07:30] Maya Chen: Yes Optimize gives token cost delta, latency delta, and suggested quantization (int8/4-bit) with expected throughput. We'll show a sample Optimize report.

[08:05] Maya Chen: Opening Optimize -> Recommendations. Here it suggests continuous batching of 50ms window for this workload and a 4-bit quantized variant of the model which saves ~40% token cost but adds 10ms to p50 latency.
[08:25] Priya Menon: We can accept that trade-off for non-realtime flows. For checkout flows we need the low-latency target.

Security & private deployments:
[09:00] Hannah Lee: If we go Private (VPC), do you still provide rollout controls and Console visibility?
[09:10] Ethan Park: Yes Private can run with our control plane or with a customer-managed control plane. You'll get full Console features, audit logs, RBAC, and KMS support.
[09:22] Hannah Lee: And how do you separate PII in logs?
[09:27] Maya Chen: We can redact fields at ingest and never persist raw tokens. You can also enable token sampling for debugging.

Edge cases & failure modes:
[10:05] Maya Chen: Here's a forced failure: I intentionally return a malformed JSON (missing closing brace). Console marks validation failed and the route policy triggered fallback to 'review' webhook.
[10:20] (demo) Event: validation_failed -> retry -> repair_model -> success
[10:30] Priya Menon: How often does repair succeed?
[10:33] Maya Chen: In our experience repair succeeds ~70-85% on minor schema issues; major semantic failures require human review. We'll run checks in your pilot.

Customer-specific discussion:
[11:00] Priya Menon: Our pipeline needs an idempotent order ingestion and must reject duplicates. Can Redwood add dedupe keys?
[11:07] Ravi Desai: Yes we support idempotency keys per webhook invocation and can attach a fingerprint computed by the route.
[11:15] Samir Khan: For training evals, can we capture model outputs and compare against ground truth in Console?
[11:22] Maya Chen: Yes, we have eval sets and metric dashboards. You can bind prompt sets to routes and get regression alerts if accuracy drops.

Prompt engineering & schema hints:
[12:10] Maya Chen: Small tip: include an explicit schema example in the prompt as an anchor — it dramatically increases correct formatting. Console provides prompt templates.
[12:22] Priya Menon: We'll share a few real examples.

Billing & pricing:
[13:05] Ethan Park: Pricing model: hosted per-token with tiers; Dedicated reserved capacity by commit; Pilot pricing we can discount for a short period. I'll send the sheet.
[13:20] Priya Menon: For pilot we want limited traffic and a sandboxed webhook endpoint.
[13:25] Ethan Park: We'll provision a sandbox project and send API keys scoped to that route.

Deep technical Q&A:
[14:00] Luca Rossi: On quantization, do you run per-layer calibration? Any impact on structured output fidelity?
[14:10] Maya Chen: We run mixed-per-channel quantization and conservative calibration for structured outputs; Optimize flags potential regressions. For critical flows you can run a regression harness in the sandbox.
[14:30] Luca Rossi: For streaming validation, is validation synchronous post-stream or can we validate partial chunks?
[14:38] Maya Chen: We do final schema validation at end-of-response but we also run incremental validators that catch obvious violations mid-stream and can request more tokens or retry.

Benchmarks & next steps planning:
[16:00] Maya Chen: Proposed pilot: 2 weeks, 1 sandbox route 'orders-extract', sample 5k messages, webhook integration to your staging ingestion, and an accuracy/regression report at end.
[16:20] Priya Menon: Sounds good. We'll need to sign an SOW for the pilot. Who owns that?
[16:25] Ethan Park: I'll send the pilot SOW and pricing.

(Discussion continues with back-and-forth, occasional crosstalk, interruptions)
[27:10] Priya Menon: Quick question — if validation fails and we fallback to a review queue, do we get the original tokens for debugging?
[27:20] Maya Chen: Yes, with RBAC controls. Raw logs can be restricted but accessible to approved roles and will be redacted per your PII rules.

[30:00] Samir Khan: Any limits on schema complexity? Our order schema has nested arrays and optional polymorphic items.
[30:10] Maya Chen: We support nested objects, polymorphism via discriminator fields, and array constraints. Very deep schemas can sometimes require chunked validation — we can help design a flattening approach.

[36:05] Luca Rossi: For our timeline — if pilot goes well, we aim to go to Dedicated for peak season in Q1. What's lead time?
[36:12] Ethan Park: Dedicated provisioning is typically 4-6 weeks depending on capacity and region. We can discuss burst options in the meantime.

[40:00] Hannah Lee: Final security note: we'll want a network diagram and evidence of SOC2, plus details on key lifecycle management.
[40:10] Ethan Park: We'll attach network diagram and SOC2 report in the security pack.

Recap & explicit next steps:
[50:00] Ethan Park: Recap — Redwood to send pilot SOW + pricing, security pack, and sandbox access. Novus to share sample payloads and confirm security requirements. Plan benchmark run next week.
[50:25] Priya Menon: Agreed. Please include estimated costs for both Hosted sandbox and Dedicated run rate.
[50:32] Ethan Park: Will do.

[52:00] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with artifacts.
[52:05] Priya Menon: Thanks all, looking forward.
[52:10] (call ends)

Notes: Transcript contains some ASR artifacts; speaker labels may be approximate. References made to Console pages, sample schema file (link shared in chat), and pilot pricing spreadsheet.
